newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES DECLINE ON KEY UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES DECLINE ON KEY UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar took a further knock against most hard currencies on Tuesday with little intervention from the central bank to bail it out, dealers said.
"We've seen some volatility in rather one-way trade and there's been a significant depreciation of the dollar," one dealer commented.

"People are becoming defensive because the buying isn't stopping. There's now an element of lack of confidence," said another, adding that most banks were hording as much foreign currency as possible to guard against being caught short.
"The Reserve Bank are coming in but not enough. We need them to come in with a big chunk and that would force those people holding onto money to offload it into the market," he said.
At around 0745 GMT, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.1600/1800 against the U.S. dollar, with banks reverting to a two-point spread. This compared with 11.1500/1600 at Monday's close.
Against sterling the local unit also lost ground to 18.2190/2625 from 18.1500/1700 but edged up slightly to 6.6550/6690 on the mark from 6.6600/6800.
Against the rand, it slipped to 2.5280/5345 from 2.5100/5300.
